newsitem.title: USA: Lands' End fiscal year-end inventory down.
newsitem.headline: Lands' End fiscal year-end inventory down.

text.p: Lands' End Inc said Thursday its year-end inventory dropped 14 percent to $142 million from $165 million at the end of fiscal 1996.

"Our continuing challenges will be to do an even better job of managing inventory to achieve a higher first-time fulfillment rate, increasing the productivity of our catalogs and offering innovative merchandise that will enable us to stand out from the crowd," Michael Smith, chief executive officer, said in a statement.
He said sales improved strongly in the last part of the fiscal third quarter, which cut its holiday season inventory.

"Because of this, we ... were unable to fill orders at our usual seasonal rate in the fourth quarter," Smith said. "For the year, we shipped 86 percent of items ordered at the time the order was placed, compared with 90 percent in the prior year."
This resulted in increases in lost sales and the cost of shipping a higher level of backorders.

Earlier, Lands' End reported earnings for the fourth quarter ended January 31 of $37.4 million or $1.15 a share, up from $25.8 million or $0.77 a year ago, which included a $1.9 million charge for the sale of a subsidiary.
Excluding the charge, the year-ago fourth quarter income was $26.9 million or $0.80 a share.

In fiscal 1997, it earned $50.9 million or $1.54 a share, which included a $1.4 million charge on the sale of a subsidiary. In fiscal 1996, it earned $30.6 million or $0.89 a share. Excluding charges, it earned $51.8 million or $1.57 a share in fiscal 1997, up from $31.7 million or $0.92 in fiscal 1996.
Sales for the quarter rose to $423.3 million from $399.5 million. For the year, sales increased to $1.12 biillion from $1.03 billion.

"Our specialty, new and international businesses all grew strongly during the year," Smith said. "Most important, we've seen a turnaround in productivity, or sales per page, in our core monthly and prospecting catalogs."
Lands' End is a direct merchant of casualwear, bed and bath products, shoes and accessories.
